title: Mud to the Ears
summary: Princess Amapola is tired of always being clean and tidy. One rainy afternoon, she discovers in the garden a joy too big for any castle.

scenes.text:
In a castle with pink towers lived Princess Amapola.

Every morning, three ladies bathed her, perfumed her and brushed her hair with a silver brush, a hundred times, until it shone like a mirror.

"Keep still, Princess!" they would say. "Don't get dirty, Princess! Don't run, Princess!"

Amapola had to sit up very straight, with her hands still and her dress without a single crease.

But inside, tucked away, she had an enormous giggle just longing to come out and play.

And every afternoon she looked out of the window at the castle woods, with their red and yellow leaves and their dirt paths.

One afternoon, the sky filled with clouds, and it began to rain.

It rained for a good while. And when it finally stopped, the whole castle went quiet: the ladies were having their nap, and the queen was reading in the library.

Amapola tiptoed down the stairs. Slowly, very slowly, she pushed open the garden door.

Outside, it smelled of wet earth. The leaves were shining. And the path through the woods was full of puddles.

Amapola took off her shoes. She took off her socks. And she wiggled her toes in the cold grass.

For the first time in her life, there was nobody to tell her no.

Amapola looked at the puddles one by one, the way you choose a cake.

And she picked the biggest.

She took a run-up, put her feet together… and jumped. Splat!

Mud flew everywhere. It splashed her face, her blue dress, her crown and even the tip of her nose.

Amapola stood still for a second.

And then out came the laughter. It came out all at once, everything she had kept tucked away for years, so loud that the birds flew out of the trees.

She jumped again. And again. And again. She covered her knees in mud, drew a mud moustache on herself and laughed until her tummy hurt.

"AMAPOLA!"

Amapola turned round.

At the edge of the garden stood the queen, her mum, with her eyes wide open. And behind her, the three ladies, with their hands on their heads.

Amapola looked down at herself. She was covered in mud from her crown to her toes. Her blue dress wasn't blue any more. It was brown, with little spots of blue.

She stood very still, waiting for the biggest telling-off in the history of telling-offs.

There was a long silence. A very, very long one.

Then the queen did something nobody expected.

She took off her shoes. She lifted up her golden dress. And she jumped into the puddle with both feet together. Splosh!

The three ladies screamed. Amapola's mouth fell open.

"I used to be a little girl who loved mud too," said the queen, chuckling. "Until somebody told me that princesses don't get dirty."

And they jumped together, mother and daughter, until night fell.

That night, bathed and warm, Amapola climbed into bed smelling of soap and of the garden. Her mum gave her a kiss and whispered in her ear:

"You can be a princess and get dirty, my love. What matters is that you're you."
